label: CORRECTION: iteration 3's 'no code component owns the stop policy' is false for fan-out. fanout-run.cjs validates stopPolicy (normalizeStopPolicy), binds it into the leaf prompt and pre-bound setup answers, passes --stop-policy on the native path, and enforces max-iterations post-dispatch via findMaxIterationsPolicyViolation, whose violation is thrown as a lineage failure carrying stopPolicyViolation. Restated P1: single-executor path only - convergence.cjs still reads no stopPolicy, so direct and /deep single-executor runs get a stop verdict from a tool blind to the policy that overrides it.

minIterations has no code owner in any path. Zero occurrences in fanout-run.cjs, convergence.cjs and reduce-state.cjs; repo-wide the identifier survives only as a ledger-event field, a legacy required-field list and tests that assert the YAML prose. The only behavioural enforcement is a side effect: under stopPolicy=max-iterations the forced-depth check requires stopReason=maxIterationsReached and iteration count equal to the cap, so an early convergence stop fails. Under the default convergence policy (fan-out fallback and every single-executor run) nothing enforces the floor.

A fan-out launched with stopPolicy=max-iterations but no per-lineage iteration cap fails every lineage only after it has run. findMaxIterationsPolicyViolation returns 'requires a positive lineage iteration cap' and has exactly one production call site, post-dispatch inside the pool completion check; normalizeStopPolicy validates the policy value and stops there, and hasIterationCap only selects prompt wording - with no cap the leaf is told to run to legal convergence, the policy the launcher intended to forbid.

The premise that a concurrent sibling run's writes appear as contested is false. isContested requires violation.baselineDirty === true, so a sibling's write to a path that was clean at baseline is a plain violation: quarantine copy, patch, containment_violation event and advisory charged to this lane. Only a path already dirty before dispatch and changed again becomes contested. Attribution is decided by when the path was dirty, not by whether another writer could be live, so two concurrent fan-out runs on one checkout cross-attribute each other's fresh edits - nothing is destroyed under the default preserve remedy, but the advisory and quarantine copy name the wrong run's work.

Both v4.0.0.16 deep-loop claims hold, with one parity gap. Resume works because the logical effect id appends :redispatch-<count>, so the gateway cannot replay the first dispatch and the executor runs again. Operator edits are contested in both paths: fan-out routes through enforceWriteContainment and emits containment_contested, and all four /deep workflow YAMLs call the same function with stateLogPath and print contested paths with their note, enforced by write-containment-yaml-call-sites.vitest.ts. The gap: restore is opt-in only via fan-out's --containment-mode / containment.mode; no single-lineage workflow accepts a containment mode, so /deep:research can only preserve.

Improvement closing f-iter004-002 and f-iter004-003: accept --min-iterations in convergence.cjs and emit minIterationsNotReached from code so the single-executor path has the floor the YAML computes by hand, and move the max-iterations cap requirement into launch validation beside normalizeStopPolicy while keeping the post-dispatch forced-depth check as the invariant of record.

label: The iteration record the prompt contract demands is not the ledger's schema, and a bad status fails opaquely. The ledger accepts status only from complete|error|insight|stuck|thought|timeout, so a correcting iteration has no honest value and the accepted fallback is insight. An out-of-vocabulary status is reported as {ok:false,phase:runtime,reason:'Payload validator rejected the event'} with exit 1 and no field, value or allowed set, because isPayload returns a boolean and the field-level throws never fire on the enum path. The legacy iteration accessor also builds its data block from status, newInfoRatio and ruledOut only, so focus and answeredQuestions never reach the canonical row and the question tick depends on the delta file alone.

P1 candidate: the gateway's authorized append refreshes the research state log from the ledger and the refresh removed rows the writers had appended - the two containment event rows (containment_contested, containment_violation) and the iteration_start row that were present before iteration 4. The projection behaves as its own contract describes, but the effect contradicts the config's append-only fileProtection entry and removes the containment audit trail that write-containment.ts calls the contested path's only durable record. Whether those rows survive in the canonical ledger is unverified; if not, the trail is lost on any later append.
